title: ERP JSON converted to a Factur-X PDF/A-3 and CII XML on staging (target EN16931)
rights: MIT; authored synthetic data, no customer input (see the manifest.json of the capture)

capture.what: date, request and HTTP status of the capture

response.what: the complete HTTP response (PDF and XML base64-encoded)

result_pdf.what: the Factur-X PDF the API returned

result_xml.what: the CII XML the API returned

oracles.what: independent checks: XSD, CEN Schematron, PDF/A-3B

cen_svrl.what: SVRL report of the official CEN EN16931 1.3.16 Schematron on the returned XML

mustang_pdf.what: Mustang / veraPDF report on the returned PDF

preservation.what: comparison of the input values with the XML and PDF output

manifest.what: sizes and SHA-256 of every published file of the capture

observed.engine: official CEN validation-1.3.16 XSLT, SaxonC-HE 12.9.0 (a second reference: the service applies the Factur-X pack for CII)

fr_ctc.reason: no France CTC validation was run or claimed in this capture

pa_acceptance.reason: a technical check never proves acceptance by a PA

runs.request: POST /api/v1/convert?enrich=false with invoice_data=invoice.json, validation_target=en16931, output=facturx_pdfa3 (a staging API key is needed to replay it)

limits: Staging at the build above, on the date above: not production, and it can change if the rules or the service change.

Five texts of the input are not kept identically in the visible PDF (for example an em dash becomes a question mark and the euro sign becomes EUR); the accents of this example do not prove support for all Unicode characters.
A text annex added to a source PDF disappeared from the returned PDF in a second test, although the response was a success (see the attachment-probe folder of the capture).
No lossless conversion, no France CTC validation, no Peppol / XRechnung conformity and no acceptance by a PA is shown by this case.
